category: RF & Wave Optics II: ports, lumped ports, network elements, RF studies, S-parameter/far-field variables and RF/optics result features
description: Waveguide, TEM, periodic and lumped ports with their subnodes, lumped/network elements, port sweeps, RF-specific study steps (Adaptive Frequency Sweep, TEM Boundary Mode Analysis, lossy eigenfrequency), the built-in S-parameter, port, periodic-structure, loss, far-field and antenna variables, Smith/polarization/radiation-pattern result features, and the ray-optics result features (spot diagram, aberrations, interference, MTF). Type strings and property names are from COMSOL 6.4 plugin definitions, the Programming Reference and Application Library models.

tools.name: Rectangular Port (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Port type with the analytic TE or TM mode field of a metallic rectangular waveguide (for example TE10) in 3D, or of a parallel-plate waveguide (TEM, TE or TM) in 2D. It launches the chosen mode with the specified input power and absorbs the same mode on the way out, so S-parameters between ports come directly. Use it for hollow-waveguide components - bends, filters, couplers, horn feeds - whose port cross-section is an air-filled or fully filled rectangle.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Port > Type of port: Rectangular. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("port1", "Port", 2); feature("port1").set("PortType", "Rectangular"); set("PortModeType", "TE"); set("PortModeNumber", "10"); set("PortExcitation", "on"); set("Pin", "1[W]")

parameters.name: PortName
parameters.description: Nonnegative integer; defines S-parameter indices, sweeps and Touchstone export.

parameters.name: PortModeType / PortModeNumber
parameters.description: TE or TM and mode indices (10 for TE10, 11 for TM11); 2D offers TEM/TE/TM with a single index.

parameters.name: PortExcitation / Pin
parameters.description: Wave excitation on/off and port input power (W in 3D/2D-axi, W/m in 2D).

parameters.name: Cutoff Frequency Calculator
parameters.description: Enter the filling relative permittivity and click Compute Waveguide Cutoff Frequency.

parameters.name: Plot Analytical Port Mode Field
parameters.description: Instant preview when the port is parallel to a Cartesian plane.

tools.notes: The port boundary must be flat with a cross-section that is constant in the normal direction. Operate above the TE10 cutoff or the mode is evanescent and S-parameters lose meaning. Only one port may be excited at a time for S-parameters; use a Port Sweep or Frequency Domain Source Sweep for the full matrix.

tools.name: Coaxial Port (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Port type with the analytic TEM mode of a coaxial line, available in 3D and 2D axisymmetry; the field is computed from the annular cross-section and needs no mode analysis. It is the standard feed for connectorized devices, coaxial filters and antennas fed through a coax, giving S-parameters referenced to the TEM mode.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Port > Type of port: Coaxial. API: feature("port1").set("PortType", "Coaxial")

parameters.name: PortType = Coaxial
parameters.description: TEM mode only (PortCoaxialModeType TEM).

parameters.name: PortExcitation / Pin / Thetap
parameters.description: Excitation on/off, input power and mode phase.

tools.notes: In 3D the port must be a full coaxial annulus; in 2D axisymmetry the azimuthal mode number must be 0. For a gap much smaller than the wavelength a Lumped Port of Coaxial type is a lighter alternative.

tools.name: Circular Port and Circular Port Reference Axis (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Port type with analytic TE or TM modes of a circular metallic waveguide (for example TE11 or TM01) in 3D and 2D axisymmetry. In 3D the Circular Port Reference Axis subnode, defined by two points, fixes the orientation of the degenerate modes - for TE11 the axis is the E-field polarization at the port center - so orthogonal polarizations can be launched and separated.
tools.usage: Port > Type of port: Circular; right-click Port > Points > Circular Port Reference Axis. API: feature("port1").set("PortType", "Circular"); set("PortModeType", "TE"); set("CircularPortModeNumber", "11"); feature("port1").create("cportv1", "CircularPortReferenceAxis", 0)

parameters.name: PortModeType / CircularPortModeNumber
parameters.description: TE or TM; mode number such as 11 (TE11) or 01 (TM01).

parameters.name: Circular Port Reference Axis (points)
parameters.description: First and last selected points define the reference direction.

parameters.name: Cutoff Frequency Calculator
parameters.description: Waveguide cutoff for the selected mode and filling permittivity.

tools.notes: Add a second port on the same boundary with the orthogonal reference axis to capture cross-polarized reflection. In 2D axisymmetry circular modes with m != 0 use the azimuthal mode number of the interface; 3D far-field norms are then available through norm3DEfar functions.

tools.name: Numeric Port with Boundary Mode Analysis (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Port type whose mode field and propagation constant are computed numerically by a Boundary Mode Analysis study step on the port boundary, so arbitrary cross-sections - ridged or dielectric-loaded waveguides, microstrip, optical fibers and integrated waveguides - can be excited and terminated. With 'Analyze as a TEM field' and an Integration Line for Voltage (plus an optional Integration Line for Current) the port also computes the mode's characteristic impedance and includes the mismatch to the reference impedance Zref.
tools.usage: Port > Type of port: Numeric; Study: add one Boundary Mode Analysis step per numeric port (Port name set) before the Frequency Domain step. API: feature("port1").set("PortType", "Numeric"); model.study("std1").create("bma", "BoundaryModeAnalysis"); model.study("std1").feature("bma").set("PortName", "1"); set("modeFreq", "7[GHz]"); set("shift", "...")

parameters.name: PortType = Numeric
parameters.description: Mode from the study; computed on the deformed mesh when a moving mesh is present.

parameters.name: Analyze as a TEM field (numericTEM) / Zref
parameters.description: 3D only; needs Integration Line for Voltage; mode field scaled by computed Zc/Zref (default 50 ohm).

parameters.name: Boundary Mode Analysis: PortName, modeFreq, neigs, shift, transform
parameters.description: Port to solve, frequency, number of modes and the search value (effective index or propagation constant).

tools.notes: For pure TE/TM/TEM modes the mode shape is frequency independent and beta is rescaled automatically, so one Boundary Mode Analysis at a reference frequency suffices; for dispersive, multi-material guides (fibers) put the mode analysis and frequency step inside a parametric sweep over frequency. Variables: emw.beta_1, emw.neff_1.

tools.name: TEM Port with Ground and Electric Potential Subnodes (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Port type (PortType TEM) for multi-conductor transmission lines such as microstrips, striplines, CPWs and differential pairs: a TEM Boundary Mode Analysis step solves an electrostatic-type problem on the port face using Ground (0 V) and Electric Potential (+1 V or -1 V) subnodes on the conductor edges, giving the mode field and the characteristic impedance from sqrt(L/C). The mode is then scaled by the ratio of the computed impedance and the reference impedance Zref.
tools.usage: Port > Type of port: Transverse electromagnetic (TEM); right-click Port > Ground / Electric Potential; Study: TEM Boundary Mode Analysis + Frequency Domain. API: feature("port1").set("PortType", "TEM"); feature("port1").create("gnd1", "Ground", 1); feature("port1").create("pot1", "ElectricPotential", 1); feature("port1").feature("pot1").set("V0", "PositiveElectricPotential")

parameters.name: Characteristic impedance Zref
parameters.description: Reference impedance, default 50 ohm.

parameters.name: Ground subnode
parameters.description: Zero potential on the selected port edges (3D) for the mode calculation.

parameters.name: Electric Potential subnode (V0)
parameters.description: PositiveElectricPotential (default) or NegativeElectricPotential (1 V).

tools.notes: Only valid for (quasi-)TEM lines with at least two conductors. Differential and common modes of a pair are obtained with +1 V/-1 V versus +1 V/+1 V potentials.

tools.name: User-Defined Port (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Port type in which the outgoing-wave mode field is typed in as an electric mode field E0 or magnetic mode field H0 together with the propagation constant beta (default emw.k, correct only for TEM-like waves). It is used for plane-wave ports in free space or in unit cells, for analytic modes not covered by the built-in types, and for fields imported from another solution; the amplitude is normalized internally.
tools.usage: Port > Type of port: User defined. API: feature("port1").set("PortType", "UserDefined"); set("E0", new String[]{"0", "0", "1"}); set("beta", "emw.k")

parameters.name: Electric mode field E0 / Magnetic mode field H0
parameters.description: Differentiable expressions (default the tangent vector t1); only tangential components matter.

parameters.name: Propagation constant beta
parameters.description: rad/m; must be a correct frequency-dependent expression for non-TEM modes.

parameters.name: Mode phase Thetap
parameters.description: Rotates the mode by a phase (enter pi to flip polarity); changes S21 but not S11 of the exciting port.

tools.example:
Plane-wave port on top of a 2D slab: set PortType = UserDefined, E0 = (0, 0, 1) (out-of-plane polarization), beta = emw.k; a second user-defined port on the bottom face listens for the transmitted wave.
Application Library: RF_Module/Verification_Examples/fresnel_equations (periodic-port alternative)
tools.notes: Since COMSOL 6.0 the mode field represents the outgoing wave; older models are migrated automatically. For oblique plane waves in periodic cells prefer the Periodic port type, which computes diffraction orders.

tools.name: Periodic Port and Periodic Port Reference Point (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Port type for unit cells of periodic structures that launches a plane wave at a given elevation/azimuth (3D) or angle of incidence (2D) with linear (TE/TM/mixed), circular or user-defined polarization, and absorbs the zero-order wave. The 'Add Diffraction Orders' action generates Diffraction Order and Orthogonal Polarization subnodes for every order that propagates, and the Periodic Port Reference Point (3D) fixes the primitive and reciprocal lattice vectors from the port edges. Used for gratings, metasurfaces, frequency selective surfaces and antireflection structures.
tools.usage: Port > Type of port: Periodic (with Periodic Condition/Floquet on the side walls), or use the Periodic Structure node which creates Periodic Port subnodes. API: feature("port1").set("PortType", "Periodic"); set("Polarization", "LinearPol"); set("LinearPol", "TE"); set("alpha1_inc", "theta"); feature("port1").runCommand("addDiffractionOrders")

parameters.name: Polarization / LinearPol / CircularPol / etaTM
parameters.description: UserDefined (default for Port), LinearPol TE|TM|Mixed with TM power fraction, CircularPol rhcp|lhcp.

parameters.name: alpha1_inc, alpha2_inc (3D) / alpha_inc (2D)
parameters.description: Elevation and azimuth angles of incidence (only on the excited port).

parameters.name: Automatic Diffraction Order Calculation
parameters.description: IncludeInAutomaticDiffractionOrderCalculation, refractive index (FromAdjacentDomain or user), DiffractionOrderSpecification (FromCurrentParameters | AllAngles), MaximumFrequency (FromStudy or fmax).

parameters.name: Periodic Port Reference Point
parameters.description: Point where the two edges spanning a1 and a2 meet; mirror it on the listener port.

tools.notes: The mode field assumes homogeneous isotropic material next to the port. Listener directions follow from the source angles and refractive indices, so several excited periodic ports with different angles make them ambiguous. Default Polarization plots and Jones-vector variables are created when all three field components are solved for.

tools.name: Diffraction Order (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Listener subnode of a periodic port that absorbs and reports the plane wave of diffraction order (m, n) with in-plane or out-of-plane polarization relative to the plane of diffraction. Each order becomes an extra port in the S-matrix, so reflectance and transmittance of individual orders (and their polarization via Jones vectors) are obtained. Normally created automatically by 'Add Diffraction Orders'.
tools.usage: Right-click a Periodic port (or Periodic Port under Periodic Structure) > Diffraction Order. API: model.component("comp1").physics("ewfd").feature("ps1").feature("pport1").create("dport3", "DiffractionOrder", 1); feature("dport3").set("mOrder", "-1"); set("components", "outofplane")

parameters.name: PortName
parameters.description: Unique integer; becomes the S-parameter index.

parameters.name: components
parameters.description: inplane (default) or outofplane polarization of the diffracted wave.

parameters.name: mOrder / nOrder
parameters.description: Integer diffraction orders (n only in 3D).

parameters.name: Mode phase Thetap
parameters.description: Phase of the mode field.

tools.notes: In 2D the reciprocal vector flips between the exciting and transmission-side ports, so order m on one side corresponds to -m on the other. The components setting follows the interface's field components when changed.

tools.name: Orthogonal Polarization (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: Listener subnode of a periodic port that captures the zero-order plane wave with the polarization orthogonal to the parent port's mode, so cross-polarized reflection and transmission (for example TE-to-TM conversion in a twisted metasurface or liquid-crystal cell) appears as its own S-parameter. Only one is allowed per periodic port and its diffraction order is fixed to zero.
tools.usage: Right-click a Periodic port > Orthogonal Polarization (usually added by Add Diffraction Orders). API: feature("port1").create("oport1", "OrthogonalPolarization", 2)

parameters.name: PortName
parameters.description: Unique integer port name.

parameters.name: Mode phase Thetap
parameters.description: Phase of the orthogonal mode field.

tools.example:
Circular-polarization converter unit cell: excite port 1 with LinearPol TE, add Orthogonal Polarization (port 3) on the listener side and plot abs(ewfd.S31)^2 versus wavelength.
Application Libraries: Wave_Optics_Module/Gratings_and_Metamaterials/hexagonal_grating, circular_polarization
tools.notes: Variables use the suffix _orth, e.g. ewfd.Rorder_0_0_orth and ewfd.Torder_0_0_orth.

tools.name: Port Options: Slit Condition, De-Embedding, Deposited Power and Mode Phase (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Advanced Port settings that change where and how a port acts. 'Activate slit condition on interior port' places a port on an interior boundary - Domain-backed (the backing domain must be homogeneous and truncated by a PML) or PEC-backed - with a toggleable power-flow direction. A nonzero port offset de-embeds the S-parameters to a reference plane (variables such as emw.dS11), 'Enable active port feedback' specifies the deposited instead of the incident power, and the mode phase rotates the mode polarity.
tools.usage: Port > Port Properties / Activate Slit Condition / De-Embedding Port sections. API: feature("port1").set("PortSlit", "1"); set("SlitType", "DomainBacked"); set("PortOffset", "5[mm]"); set("SpecifyDepositedPower", "1"); set("Pdep", "1[kW]"); set("Thetap", "pi")

parameters.name: PortSlit / SlitType / TogglePowerFlowDirection
parameters.description: Interior port; DomainBacked (default) or PECBacked; arrow shows power flow (into the excited domain for an inport).

parameters.name: PortOffset (doffset)
parameters.description: De-embedding distance along a straight uniform section; phase corrected with beta.

parameters.name: SpecifyDepositedPower / Pdep
parameters.description: Input power adjusted so that the non-reflected power equals Pdep; this must be the only inport.

parameters.name: Thetap
parameters.description: Mode phase in rad.

tools.notes: Unmatched outgoing power on a domain-backed slit port is reported by emw.PoutNMPort_N. De-embedding assumes the section between port and reference plane is straight with constant cross-section.

tools.name: Lumped Port Types and Terminal Types (Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain)
tools.description: The Lumped Port node offers six geometric types - Uniform (rectangular gap), Coaxial, Multielement uniform (several subelements, e.g. CPW or differential feeds), Reference-edge controlled, Via (plated through hole) and User defined (height, width and field direction of a curved gap) - and three terminal types: Cable (voltage-driven transmission line with S-parameters), Current and Circuit (connected to an Electrical Circuit). Cable ports can be driven by a voltage V0 with phase or by an average power P0 and use a characteristic impedance Zref.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Lumped Port. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("lport1", "LumpedPort", 2); feature("lport1").set("PortType", "Uniform"); set("TerminalType", "Cable"); set("PortExcitation", "on"); set("SourceType", "Voltage"); set("V0", "1[V]"); set("Zref", "50[ohm]")

parameters.name: PortType
parameters.description: Uniform, Coaxial, UserDefined (hPort, wPort, ahPort), Via, Multielement uniform, Reference-edge controlled.

parameters.name: TerminalType
parameters.description: Cable (default), Current (I0) or Circuit.

parameters.name: SourceType / V0 / Thetap / P0
parameters.description: Voltage (with port phase) or Power source when PortExcitation is on.

parameters.name: Zref / AdjustZref
parameters.description: Characteristic impedance; option to enter the full-geometry value when symmetry planes cut the port.

parameters.name: Split by Connectivity / Coaxial Line Impedance Calculator / Reverse mode field direction
parameters.description: Helper actions.

tools.notes: The port must bridge two metallic boundaries (PEC, IBC, TBC, layered TBC or Cable Shield) separated by much less than a wavelength. In a half-symmetry model without Symmetry Plane nodes, scale Zref with the cut (half coax -> twice the impedance). A generic Lumped Port entry also exists in this catalog.

tools.name: Lumped Element (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Passive lumped-port-like boundary that inserts an impedance between two metallic boundaries to mimic a chip resistor, capacitor, inductor or LC/RLC network without meshing the component. It cannot be a source and produces no S-parameters; its current and power have the opposite sign convention to a Lumped Port. Typical uses are termination resistors in power dividers, tuning capacitors and ESD test loads.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Lumped Element. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("lelement1", "LumpedElement", 2); feature("lelement1").set("LumpedElementType", "UserDefinedImpedance"); set("Zelement", "100[ohm]")

parameters.name: LumpedElementType
parameters.description: UserDefinedImpedance (default), Inductor, Capacitor, Parallel LC, Series LC, Parallel RLC, Series RLC (L/C/RLC types only in the frequency domain).

parameters.name: Zelement / Lelement / Celement / Relement
parameters.description: Defaults 50 ohm, 1 nH, 1 pF, 50 ohm.

parameters.name: PortType / hPort / wPort / ahPort
parameters.description: Same geometric types as the Lumped Port (Uniform, Coaxial, User defined, ...).

tools.notes: In Electromagnetic Waves, Transient only the user-defined impedance is available. For frequency-dependent networks characterized by measured data use Two-Port Network with a Touchstone file.

tools.name: Uniform Element (Multielement Uniform Lumped Port subnode)
tools.description: Subnode of a Lumped Port of type Multielement uniform that defines one sub-gap of the port and the direction between its terminals (the electric-field direction, which sets the potential polarity). Several uniform elements together excite a coplanar waveguide (both slots at once) or a differential/balanced feed as one port.
tools.usage: Lumped Port (Type of lumped port: Multielement uniform) > right-click > Uniform Element (3D). API: feature("lport1").create("ue1", "UniformElement", 2); feature("lport1").feature("ue1").set("ahUniformElement", new String[]{"1", "0", "0"})

parameters.name: Uniform element name
parameters.description: Unique name.

parameters.name: Direction between uniform element terminals (ahUniformElement)
parameters.description: Points in the direction of the electric field in the sub-gap.

tools.example:
CPW feed: Lumped Port 1 of type Multielement uniform with Uniform Element 1 on the left slot (ah = (-1,0,0)) and Uniform Element 2 on the right slot (ah = (1,0,0)) so both slots are driven from the center conductor outward.
Application Library: RF_Module/Filters/cpw_bandpass_filter
tools.notes: Available in 3D only.

tools.name: Two-Port Network (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Boundary feature that inserts a two-port black box, characterized by S-parameters, between two lumped-port-like boundaries of the field model; the two terminals are the default Two-Port Network Port subnodes. The S-matrix is either a constant matrix with a reference impedance or is read from a two-port Touchstone file and interpolated over the simulation frequencies. It lets measured or vendor-supplied components (filters, amplifier stages, chip parts) be embedded in a 3D full-wave model.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Two-Port Network; select the boundaries of each terminal in Two-Port Network Port 1 and 2. Type strings: TwoPortNetwork (tpn), subnodes Two-Port Network Port.

parameters.name: Type of Port
parameters.description: Coaxial or Uniform (coaxial requires azimuthal mode number 0 in 2D-axi).

parameters.name: Type of S-parameter Definition
parameters.description: Matrix (with characteristic impedance Zref) or Touchstone file (.s2p).

parameters.name: Interpolation
parameters.description: Nearest neighbor, Linear, Piecewise cubic (default) or Cubic spline within the file's frequency range.

parameters.name: Extrapolation
parameters.description: Constant (default), Linear, Nearest function or Specific value outside the range.

tools.example:
Filter characterized by a measured .s2p file placed between two microstrip lines:
1. Two-Port Network 1 > Type of Port: Uniform; S-parameter definition: Touchstone file > browse filter.s2p.
2. Two-Port Network Port 1/2: select the two gap boundaries.
Application Library: RF_Module/Filters/two_port_network_touchstone
tools.notes: Terminals must span two metallic boundaries separated by much less than a wavelength (PEC, IBC or TBC).

tools.name: Three-Port Network and Four-Port Network (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Three- and four-terminal versions of the network black box: S-parameters from a constant matrix or a .s3p/.s4p Touchstone file characterize the reflection and transmission between three or four lumped terminals defined by Three-Port Network Port or Four-Port Network Port subnodes. Use them to embed circulators, couplers, baluns or measured multi-port packages into a full-wave model.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Boundaries > Three-Port Network / Four-Port Network. Type strings: ThreePortNetwork (trpn), FourPortNetwork (fpn).

parameters.name: Type of Port
parameters.description: Coaxial or Uniform.

parameters.name: Type of S-parameter Definition
parameters.description: Matrix (with Zref) or Touchstone file.

parameters.name: Interpolation / Extrapolation
parameters.description: Same options as Two-Port Network.

tools.example: Measured hybrid coupler (.s4p) connected to four microstrip feed lines of an antenna array: Four-Port Network 1 > Touchstone file; assign the four gap boundaries to Four-Port Network Port 1-4 in the same order as the file.
tools.notes: Port order in the Touchstone file must match the subnode order.

tools.name: Mixed-Mode S-Parameters (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Global feature that converts the full 4x4 single-ended S-matrix of a four-port device into differential-mode, common-mode and mode-conversion S-parameters for two balanced pairs. It is used for differential interconnects, balanced filters and signal-integrity analysis, producing variables such as emw.Sdd21dB, emw.Scc11dB, emw.Scd12dB and emw.Sdc21dB.
tools.usage: Physics toolbar > Global > Mixed-Mode S-Parameters; requires a port sweep over all four ports. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").create("mms1", "MixedModeSparameters", -1); feature("mms1").set("portA", "1"); set("portB", "3"); set("portC", "2"); set("portD", "4")

parameters.name: portA / portB
parameters.description: Port names of balanced pair 1.

parameters.name: portC / portD
parameters.description: Port names of balanced pair 2.

tools.notes: Port names must match those of the (lumped) ports; without a complete 4x4 matrix the mixed-mode values are meaningless.

tools.name: Port Sweep Settings (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: Interface-level option that runs a parametric sweep over the port names on top of the frequency sweep, exciting one port at a time so the complete S-parameter matrix is assembled, and optionally writes it to a Touchstone file. The Configure Sweep Settings button creates the sweep parameter and a Parametric Sweep study step automatically. It exists in emw, Beam Envelopes, Boundary Elements, Transient and Transmission Line interfaces.
tools.usage: Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain > Port Sweep Settings > Use manual port sweep, then Configure Sweep Settings. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").prop("PortSweepSettings").set("useSweep", true); prop("PortSweepSettings").set("PortParamName", "PortName"); prop("PortSweepSettings").set("ExportTouchstone", true)

parameters.name: useSweep / PortParamName
parameters.description: Enable manual port sweep and name of the global parameter holding the excited port number (default PortName).

parameters.name: ExportTouchstone / TouchstoneFile
parameters.description: Write the S-matrix after solving.

parameters.name: Parameter format (format)
parameters.description: Magnitude angle (MA, default), Magnitude (dB) angle or Real imaginary.

parameters.name: Reference impedance zref / IfFileExists
parameters.description: Header impedance (default 50 ohm); Overwrite or Create new.

tools.notes: Port names must be numeric. The Frequency Domain Source Sweep study step is a more efficient alternative that reuses the factorization for all sources; the Touchstone export node under Results is catalogued separately.

tools.name: Adaptive Frequency Sweep (AWE)
tools.description: Study step (type FrequencyAdaptive) that computes a frequency response with a very fine frequency resolution at close to the cost of a coarse sweep, using asymptotic waveform evaluation: moment matching with Pade approximants or Taylor expansions of the transfer function, refined until user or physics-controlled scalar expressions agree within a relative tolerance. It is ideal for high-Q single-resonance filters, antennas and couplers; the same AWE solver can be switched on in Frequency Domain and Wavelength Domain steps under Study Extensions.
tools.usage: Add Study > Adaptive Frequency Sweep (RF, Wave Optics, MEMS or Acoustics Module). API: model.study("std1").create("frawe", "FrequencyAdaptive"); model.study("std1").feature("frawe").set("plist", "range(f1,1[MHz],f2)"); set("awefunctype", "usercontrolled"); setIndex("awefunc", "abs(comp1.emw.S21)", 0)

parameters.name: plist / punit
parameters.description: Output frequencies (can be very dense).

parameters.name: awefunctype
parameters.description: Physics controlled (default) or usercontrolled with a table of AWE expressions (awefunc).

parameters.name: rtol
parameters.description: Relative tolerance for agreement of the expansions.

parameters.name: Store fields in output (outputmap/outputselectionmap)
parameters.description: Store only port boundaries to keep the file small when only S-parameters are needed.

tools.notes: Choose smooth expressions: abs(S21) for two-port filters, abs(S11) or sqrt(1-abs(S11)^2) for antennas; an expression with an infinitely sharp dip needs many expansion points. For multi-resonance passbands the Frequency Domain, Modal method is usually faster.

tools.name: TEM Boundary Mode Analysis
tools.description: Preprocessing study step (type TEMBoundaryModeAnalysis) that solves for the static electric potential (or out-of-plane magnetic vector potential) on all TEM-type ports to define their mode shapes and characteristic impedances before the main Frequency Domain step. As a preset study it combines the TEM Boundary Mode Analysis step with a Frequency Domain step for the full geometry.
tools.usage: Add Study > TEM Boundary Mode Analysis (or add the step before Frequency Domain). API: model.study("std1").create("tbma", "TEMBoundaryModeAnalysis"); model.study("std1").create("freq", "Frequency")

parameters.name: Physics and variables selection
parameters.description: Standard study-step sections; the step acts on ports of type TEM.

tools.notes: Requires Ground and Electric Potential subnodes on each TEM port. For general (non-TEM) numeric ports use Boundary Mode Analysis instead.

tools.name: Eigenfrequency Q-Factor and Lossy Eigenvalue Settings (Electromagnetic Waves)
tools.description: For lossy or open resonators the Eigenfrequency study returns complex eigenvalues lambda = -j*omega + delta, from which the interfaces define the eigenfrequency, the damping and the quality factor Q = omega/(2|delta|) (variable emw.Qfactor or ewfd.Qfactor). Impedance boundaries with finite conductivity, scattering boundaries next to conductive domains and analytic ports make the eigenproblem nonlinear in lambda; the solver then linearizes around the 'Search for eigenfrequencies around' value, which can be changed in the Eigenvalue Solver ('Transform eigenvalue linearization point') and iterated for accuracy.
tools.usage: Add Study > Eigenfrequency; evaluate emw.Qfactor, emw.freq and emw.damp in a Global Evaluation. API: model.study("std1").create("eig", "Eigenfrequency"); feature("eig").set("neigs", 6); set("shift", "3.3[GHz]"); set("eigwhich", "lr")

parameters.name: neigs / shift
parameters.description: Desired number of eigenfrequencies and search center (also the default linearization point for nonlinear eigenproblems).

parameters.name: eigwhich
parameters.description: Search method around the shift, e.g. lr (larger real part) as recommended before a Frequency Domain, Modal step.

parameters.name: eigmethod region / eigsr, eiglr, eigsi, eigli
parameters.description: Region search bounds in the complex plane.

parameters.name: Transform eigenvalue linearization point (Eigenvalue Solver)
parameters.description: Manual linearization value for IBC/SBC/port nonlinearity.

tools.notes: Spurious modes can appear; filter them with an expression (filtereigexpression) or check field plots. An Eigenfrequency step followed by Frequency Domain, Modal gives fast multi-resonance filter responses; if not all relevant modes are included, only phase-independent S-parameter magnitudes are reliable.

tools.name: S-Parameter Variables (emw.S11, emw.S21dB, VSWR, ABCD)
tools.description: Global variables generated by Port, Lumped Port and Diffraction Order features: complex S-parameters named from the numeric port names (emw.S11, emw.S21, ...) and their dB values emw.S11dB = 20*log10(|S11|), plus emw.VSWR_N for a single excited port, the two-port ABCD matrix (emw.ABCD and emw.ABCD_A..D, from a 50 ohm port sweep or assuming reciprocity), emw.Gamma_N reflection coefficients when all ports are excited simultaneously (phased arrays) and de-embedded emw.dS11 when a port offset is set.
tools.usage: Results > Global Evaluation / 1D Plot Group > Global with expressions such as emw.S11dB, emw.S21, emw.VSWR_1; full scope comp1.emw.S21. The default 'S-parameter' plot and a Port Probe (emw_port1_probe) are created automatically.

parameters.name: emw.Sij / emw.SijdB
parameters.description: i = listener port name, j = excited port name.

parameters.name: emw.VSWR_N
parameters.description: Voltage standing wave ratio of the single excited port N.

parameters.name: emw.ABCD, emw.ABCD_A ... emw.ABCD_D
parameters.description: Two-port ABCD parameters (50 ohm reference).

parameters.name: emw.Gamma_N
parameters.description: Reflection coefficient with multiple excitation.

parameters.name: emw.dSij
parameters.description: De-embedded S-parameters (port offset).

tools.notes: S-parameter output is switched off when more than one port is excited. For wave optics the same variables exist with the ewfd/ewbe prefix, e.g. ewbe.S21.

tools.name: Port Mode Field and Propagation Constant Variables (emw.beta_1, emw.neff_1)
tools.description: Variables describing port modes and waveguide eigenmodes: for each port K the propagation constant emw.beta_K, effective mode index emw.neff_K, tangential and full electric/magnetic mode fields (emw.tEmodex_K, emw.EmodeX_K, emw.normtEmode_K, emw.Enmode_K and H counterparts). Mode Analysis defines emw.beta (propagation constant), emw.dampz and emw.dampzdB (attenuation per meter) and the complex effective index emw.neff; Boundary Mode Analysis gives complex beta_i = j*lambda and neff_i = beta_i/k0.
tools.usage: Evaluate on the port boundary or globally after a Boundary Mode Analysis / Mode Analysis step, e.g. Global Evaluation of emw.neff_1 or a Surface plot of emw.normtEmode_1.

parameters.name: emw.beta_K / emw.neff_K
parameters.description: Port K propagation constant and effective index.

parameters.name: emw.tEmodex_K, emw.EmodeX_K, emw.normEmode_K
parameters.description: Mode field components and norms (C = x, y, z or r, phi, z).

parameters.name: emw.beta, emw.dampz, emw.dampzdB, emw.neff
parameters.description: Mode Analysis results; imag(neff) > 0 indicates loss.

tools.example:
Beam Envelopes directional coupler: the propagation constants from the Boundary Mode Analysis steps are reused as wave vectors, e.g. k1 = (ewbe.beta_1, 0, 0) and k2 = (ewbe2.beta_2, ewbe2.k1y, ewbe2.k1z).
Application Libraries: Wave_Optics_Module/Couplers_Filters_and_Mirrors/directional_coupler, RF_Module/Verification_Examples/coaxial_cable_impedance
tools.notes: In 2D axisymmetric mode analysis the relation between eigenvalue and neff involves the scaling radius set in the interface. Mode Analysis and Boundary Mode Analysis study steps are catalogued separately.

tools.name: Lumped Port Variables (emw.Vport_1, emw.Iport_1, emw.Zport_1)
tools.description: Each lumped port N defines the extracted port voltage emw.Vport_N (line integral of E across the gap, averaged over the port), the port current emw.Iport_N (averaged over cross-sections parallel to the terminals) and the port impedance emw.Zport_N = Vport/Iport, from which S11 follows with the reference impedance. These give antenna input impedance, resonance and matching directly and are also defined in the transient interfaces (for example temw.Vport_1 for crosstalk or TDR).
tools.usage: Global Evaluation / Global plot of real(emw.Zport_1), imag(emw.Zport_1), emw.Vport_1; in time domain temw.Vport_2 versus t.

parameters.name: emw.Vport_N
parameters.description: Extracted port voltage.

parameters.name: emw.Iport_N
parameters.description: Port current.

parameters.name: emw.Zport_N
parameters.description: Port impedance (input impedance of the device seen from the port).

tools.example:
Dipole input impedance versus frequency: 1D Plot Group > Global with expressions real(emw.Zport_1) and imag(emw.Zport_1).
Application Libraries: RF_Module/Antennas/dipole_antenna, RF_Module/EMI_EMC_Applications/microstrip_line_crosstalk (temw.Vport_1..4)
tools.notes: Non-excited ports only return voltage and current. The values are meaningful only when the gap is much smaller than the wavelength.

tools.name: Periodic Structure and Diffraction Order Variables (emw.Rorder_0_0, emw.RTtotal)
tools.description: Periodic ports and diffraction orders define diffraction efficiencies per order and totals: reflectance and transmittance of order (m, n) as tag.Rorder_m_n and tag.Torder_m_n (with _ip/_op for in-plane/out-of-plane polarization and _orth for the orthogonal polarization, negative orders written n1, positive p1), per-port Rport_N/Tport_N, the totals Rtotal, Ttotal and RTtotal (energy balance check) and absorptance Atotal. Geometric variables give diffraction angles (alpha1R_m_n, alpha2T_m_n), mode wave vectors (kModex_K), unit-cell axes, reference directions, primitive and reciprocal lattice vectors.
tools.usage: Global Evaluation or Global plot versus wavelength/angle, e.g. ewfd.Rorder_0_0, ewfd.Torder_n1_0_ip, ewfd.RTtotal; lattice vectors emw.b1x, emw.G1x; angles emw.alpha1R_0_0.

parameters.name: Rorder_m_n / Torder_m_n (_ip, _op, _orth)
parameters.description: Diffraction efficiency of an order; 2D uses a single index (Rorder_n1).

parameters.name: Rtotal, Ttotal, RTtotal, Atotal
parameters.description: Total reflectance, transmittance, their sum and total absorptance.

parameters.name: Rport_N / Tport_N
parameters.description: Reflectance/transmittance for port N.

parameters.name: alpha1R_m_n, alpha2R_m_n, alpha1T_m_n, kModex_K, Eamplx_K
parameters.description: Elevation/azimuth of each order, mode wave vector and amplitude.

parameters.name: axisx, aUnit1x, b1x, G1x (and R/T variants)
parameters.description: Unit-cell axis, reference directions, primitive and reciprocal lattice vectors.

tools.example:
Wire-grid polarizer: plot ewfd.Rorder_0, ewfd.Torder_0 and ewfd.RTtotal versus lambda0 after a Wavelength Domain sweep; 1 - RTtotal equals the absorbed fraction.
Application Libraries: Wave_Optics_Module/Applications/plasmonic_wire_grating, Wave_Optics_Module/Gratings_and_Metamaterials/metasurface_beam_deflector, hexagonal_grating
tools.notes: Order variables exist only for orders that have Diffraction Order ports; use 'Add Diffraction Orders' with 'All angles' when sweeping the incidence angle.

tools.name: Jones Vector Variables (emw.JIOOP_0_0, emw.normJR_0_0)
tools.description: For periodic ports, when all three field components are solved for, the interfaces expand each plane-wave order in an out-of-plane (e1 = k x n) and in-plane (e2 = e1 x k) basis and store the complex, non-normalized Jones vector elements as global variables. Names encode the side (I input, R reflection side, T transmission side), the polarization (OOP or IP) and the order, for example emw.JIOOP_0_n1 or ewfd.JTIP_p1_p1; norms are tag.normJR_m_n and basis vectors tag.eJRIPx_m_n.
tools.usage: Global Evaluation of arg(emw.JROOP_0_0)-arg(emw.JRIP_0_0) (phase difference) or abs values; default Polarization plots use these variables.

parameters.name: tag.JXYYY_Z
parameters.description: X = I/R/T, YYY = OOP/IP, Z = order (2D: signed integer, 3D: m_n with p/n prefixes).

parameters.name: tag.normJX_Z
parameters.description: Norm of the Jones vector of that order.

parameters.name: tag.eJXYYY[x,y,z]_Z
parameters.description: Basis vector components on the port boundaries.

tools.example:
Quarter-wave metasurface check: evaluate abs(ewfd.JTOOP_0_0)/abs(ewfd.JTIP_0_0) (should be 1) and the phase difference (should be +-pi/2 for circular output).
Application Libraries: RF_Module/Tutorials/hexagonal_grating, Wave_Optics_Module/Gratings_and_Metamaterials/frequency_selective_surface_csrr
tools.notes: Equal phases (or pi apart) mean linear polarization, +-pi/2 circular, anything else elliptical.

tools.name: Coupling, Outcoupling and Loss Variables (emw.Pin, emw.Pout, emw.Atotal)
tools.description: Power-balance variables of the Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain interface: input power emw.Pin from ports or scattering-boundary incident fields, outgoing power per feature and in total (emw.sctr1.Pout, emw.port1.Pout, emw.wee1.pml1.Pout, emw.Pout), outcoupling efficiencies (emw.port1.etaOut, emw.etaOut), scattering losses (emw.Lsca, emw.LscaPort_N), absorbed power per lossy feature (emw.wee1.Ploss, emw.imp1.Ploss, emw.trans1.Ploss, emw.Ploss) and absorptances (emw.imp1.A, emw.Atotal). They make energy-conservation checks and efficiency studies one-line evaluations.
tools.usage: Global Evaluation of emw.Pin, emw.Pout, emw.Ploss, emw.Atotal or feature-scoped names such as emw.sctr1.Pout.

parameters.name: emw.Pin
parameters.description: Defined only for driven studies with a Full field formulation and an input from Port or Scattering Boundary Condition.

parameters.name: Pout family
parameters.description: Also PoutMPort_N (matched) and PoutNMPort_N (non-matched, domain-backed slit ports).

parameters.name: etaOut family
parameters.description: Pout/Pin for each feature and in total; emw.portM.etaOut = abs(emw.SN1)^2.

parameters.name: Ploss / A / Atotal / Lsca
parameters.description: Absorbed power, absorptance and scattering-loss variables.

tools.example:
Waveguide S-bend loss budget: evaluate ewfd.etaOutPort_2 (transmitted), ewfd.Lsca (radiated into PML) and ewfd.Atotal (absorbed); their sum with the reflected part should be 1.
Application Libraries: Wave_Optics_Module/Waveguides/waveguide_s_bend, Ray_Optics_Module/Verification_Examples/diffraction_grating (ewfd.Atotal)
tools.notes: Outgoing-power variables are defined for all study types and both formulations, but outcoupling needs Pin. Scattering Boundary Condition output is not counted as scattering loss.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Field, Power Flow and Loss Density Variables (emw.normE, emw.Poavx, emw.Qrh)
tools.description: Field-level postprocessing variables of the electromagnetic-wave interfaces: field components and norms (emw.Ex, emw.normE, emw.Hx, emw.normH, emw.normB, 2D-axi emw.Ephi), the time-averaged Poynting vector emw.Poavx/y/z and its normal component emw.nPoav on boundaries, the resistive loss density emw.Qrh, the surface loss density emw.Qsh on impedance boundaries, energy variables such as emw.Wav and the integrated energies emw.intWe/emw.intWm, surface currents emw.Jsx and emw.normJs, and in scattered-field models the relative/background fields (emw.relEz, emw.Ebz).
tools.usage: Surface/Slice/Multislice plots (default 'Electric Field' plot uses emw.normE), Line Graph of emw.nPoav, Volume Integration of emw.Qrh over a load domain, Global Evaluation of emw.intWe.

parameters.name: emw.normE / emw.Ex ...
parameters.description: Electric field magnitude and components (complex amplitudes; plots show the real part at phase 0).

parameters.name: emw.Poavx, emw.nPoav
parameters.description: Time-average power flow density and its normal component (W/m^2).

parameters.name: emw.Qrh / emw.Qsh
parameters.description: Resistive volume loss density (W/m^3) and surface loss density (W/m^2).

parameters.name: emw.Wav, emw.intWe, emw.intWm
parameters.description: Energy density and integrated electric/magnetic energy, used e.g. in Q = omega*W/P estimates.

parameters.name: emw.relEz / emw.Ebz
parameters.description: Relative (scattered) and background field in the scattered-field formulation.

tools.example:
Absorbed power in a food load: Derived Values > Volume Integration of emw.Qrh over the load domains; cross-check with emw.wee2.Ploss.
Application Libraries: RF_Module/Microwave_Heating/microwave_oven (emw.Qrh), RF_Module/Verification_Examples/cavity_resonators (emw.Qsh, emw.Wav)
tools.notes: Use the same prefix pattern for other interfaces (ewfd., ewbe., temw., ewt.). To animate the time-harmonic field, sweep the Phase in the dataset or plot group.

tools.name: Far-Field Variables (emw.normEfar, emw.normdBEfar, emw.bRCS3D)
tools.description: Variables and functions generated by a Far-Field Calculation feature (default name Efar): far-field components emw.Efarx/y/z (and Efarr, Efartheta, Efarphi, EfarRHCP, EfarLHCP), the norm emw.normEfar and its dB value emw.normdBEfar, axial ratio emw.axialRatio/axialRatiodB, bistatic and monostatic radar cross section emw.bRCS3D/emw.mRCS3D (3D) or emw.bRCS2D/emw.mRCS2D per unit length (2D). Each variable also exists as a function of the direction vector, e.g. Efarx(dx,dy,dz), and in an '_opt' version for use in optimization objectives.
tools.usage: Radiation Pattern plots (3D, polar or 1D), Global Evaluation or function calls such as emw.normEfar evaluated in a Radiation Pattern with sampled theta/phi; Efarx(sin(theta)*cos(phi), sin(theta)*sin(phi), cos(theta)).

parameters.name: normEfar / normdBEfar
parameters.description: Far-field norm (V) and dB value; 2D, 2D-axi, 3D.

parameters.name: Efarx, Efary, Efarz / Efartheta, Efarphi
parameters.description: Cartesian and spherical components.

parameters.name: EfarRHCP, EfarLHCP, axialRatio, axialRatiodB
parameters.description: Circular-polarization decomposition and axial ratio (3D).

parameters.name: bRCS3D, mRCS3D, bRCS2D, mRCS2D
parameters.description: Radar cross sections for scattered-field models.

tools.example:
Monostatic RCS of a sphere versus frequency: scattered-field emw with a plane wave, Far-Field Domain/Calculation inside the PML, then Global Evaluation of emw.bRCS3D in the backscatter direction.
Application Libraries: RF_Module/Verification_Examples/rcs_sphere, RF_Module/Scattering_and_RCS/radar_cross_section (emw.mRCS2D)
tools.notes: The name prefix follows the Far-field variable name setting (Efar by default). Symmetry settings in the Far-Field Calculation must match the symmetry-plane conditions or the pattern of the full structure will be wrong.

tools.name: Antenna Gain, Directivity and Radiated Power Variables (emw.rGaindBEfar, emw.maxD, emw.TRP)
tools.description: Antenna figures of merit derived from the far field: realized gain emw.rGainEfar/rGaindBEfar = 4*pi*U/Pin, gain emw.gainEfar/gaindBEfar = 4*pi*U/Pdelivered with Pdelivered = Pin*(1-|S11|^2), maximum directivity/gain/realized gain (emw.maxD, maxDdB, maxGain, maxGaindB, maxRGain, maxRGaindB), circular-polarization realized gains (rGainRHCP, rGaindBLHCP), total radiated power emw.TRP/TRPdB and effective isotropic radiated power emw.EIRP/EIRPdB. A default realized-gain radiation pattern is created when the model is driven by ports.
tools.usage: Global Evaluation of emw.maxDdB, emw.TRP; Radiation Pattern plot of emw.rGaindBEfar; optimization objectives with the _opt variants (e.g. maxRGain_opt).

parameters.name: gainEfar / gaindBEfar
parameters.description: Gain; valid only with a single excited port (needs S11).

parameters.name: rGainEfar / rGaindBEfar
parameters.description: Realized gain including mismatch.

parameters.name: maxD, maxGain, maxRGain (+dB)
parameters.description: Evaluated via Global Evaluation; the far-field surface must be a sphere (3D) or circle (2D-axi) centered at the origin.

parameters.name: TRP, EIRP (+dB)
parameters.description: Total radiated and equivalent isotropic radiated power.

tools.example:
Patch antenna: Radiation Pattern in a Polar Plot Group with expression emw.rGaindBEfar at phi = 0 and 90 deg; Global Evaluation of emw.maxRGaindB over an Adaptive Frequency Sweep.
Application Libraries: RF_Module/Antenna_Arrays/microstrip_patch_antenna_inset, RF_Module/Antennas/conical_horn_lens_antenna_shape_optimization
tools.notes: Directivity can also be computed from a 3D Radiation Pattern plot using the squared far-field norm. Gains are 2D-axi/3D only.

tools.name: Array Factor Operators (emw.af3, emw.af2, emw.afhex)
tools.description: Far-field functions that multiply a single-element radiation pattern by the array factor of a uniform array, so the pattern of a large phased array is estimated from one element (or one periodic unit cell) without modeling the full array. af3 covers three-dimensional uniform arrays, af2 planar ones and afhex hexagonal (triangular-lattice) arrays in 3D; element spacings are given in wavelengths and progressive phase shifts in radians for beam steering.
tools.usage: Use inside a Radiation Pattern expression, e.g. emw.normEfar*emw.af3(nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, alphax, alphay, alphaz); functions are listed under Component > Definitions > Functions.

parameters.name: nx, ny, nz
parameters.description: Number of elements along x, y, z (dimensionless).

parameters.name: dx, dy, dz
parameters.description: Element spacing in wavelengths (typical 0.5).

parameters.name: alphax, alphay, alphaz
parameters.description: Phase progression in radians (steering).

parameters.name: afhex(np, dx, dy)
parameters.description: np = elements along the diagonal; odd np gives 3n^2-3n+1 elements with n = (np+1)/2.

tools.example:
8x8 patch array steered 20 deg in x: Radiation Pattern expression emw.normdBEfar + 20*log10(abs(emw.af3(8, 8, 1, 0.5, 0.5, 0, -pi*sin(20[deg]), 0, 0))).
Application Library: RF_Module/Antenna_Arrays/microstrip_patch_antenna_inset
tools.notes: Mutual coupling and edge effects are ignored; for accurate finite-array patterns model the array (possibly with BEM) or use a periodic cell with Floquet conditions. See also the Array Factor dataset.

tools.name: Array Factor (Results dataset)
tools.description: Dataset that wraps a solution dataset and applies a uniform array factor to a far-field expression in a chosen plane, so Radiation Pattern plots can show the pattern of a periodic antenna array (with array size, phase shift for steering and element displacement) computed from one element. It supports dB scaling and normalization with respect to the number of power inputs.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > More Datasets > Array Factor; select it as dataset of a Radiation Pattern plot. API: model.result().dataset().create("af1", "ArrayFactor"); dataset("af1").set("data", "dset1"); set("plane", "xy"); set("function", "emw.af3"); set("scale", "dB")

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Source dataset.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description: xy (default), yz or zx.

parameters.name: size / phaseshift / displ
parameters.description: Array size (integers), phase shift (rad, can be a sweep parameter) and displacement (fractions of the wavelength); set with setIndex.

parameters.name: function / scale / normalization
parameters.description: Array factor function (typically emw.af3), linear or dB, normalize by number of inputs.

tools.notes: Requires the RF Module license for the af3 function.

tools.name: 3D Far-Field Norm Functions in 2D Axisymmetry (emw.norm3DEfar)
tools.description: Functions norm3DEfar and normdB3DEfar that reconstruct the full 3D far-field norm of a 2D axisymmetric model with nonzero azimuthal mode, combining the positive and negative azimuthal modes, so a circular-port-fed horn or a body of revolution illuminated by a circularly polarized plane wave can be plotted as a true 3D pattern. The function suffix encodes the circular port mode, e.g. norm3DEfar_TE12 for azimuthal mode 1 and TE mode number 2; the argument is the azimuth angle.
tools.usage: 3D Radiation Pattern plot with expression emw.norm3DEfar_TE11(phi) (argument equal to the plot's azimuth angle variable), or a polar plot with a fixed argument (0 = xz-plane, pi/2 = yz-plane).

parameters.name: Argument
parameters.description: Azimuthal angle phi in radians.

parameters.name: Suffix
parameters.description: Port mode type and number combined with the azimuthal mode number of the interface.

tools.example:
Corrugated circular horn in 2D-axi with a TE11 circular port (m = 1): E-plane pattern emw.normdB3DEfar_TE11(0) and H-plane emw.normdB3DEfar_TE11(pi/2) in a Polar Plot Group.
Application Library: RF_Module/Antennas/corrugated_circular_horn_antenna
tools.notes: Available only for circular-port excitation with positive azimuthal mode number or for the predefined circularly polarized background wave.

tools.name: Reflection, Impedance and Admittance Graphs (Smith Plot Group)
tools.description: Plot types for the Smith Plot Group: the Reflection Graph plots complex reflection coefficients such as emw.S11 on the Smith chart, the Impedance Graph plots impedances normalized by a reference impedance and the Admittance Graph plots admittances with a reference admittance. Multiple expressions can share one chart, and Color Expression or Filter subnodes color the trace by frequency or restrict it; Graph Marker subnodes annotate points.
tools.usage: Results > Smith Plot Group > Reflection Graph / Impedance Graph / Admittance Graph. API: model.result().create("pg3", "SmithGroup"); model.result("pg3").create("rgr1", "ReflectionGraph"); model.result("pg3").feature("rgr1").set("expr", new String[]{"emw.S11"}); model.result("pg3").create("ig1", "ImpedanceGraph"); model.result("pg3").create("ag1", "AdmittanceGraph")

parameters.name: expr / descr
parameters.description: Expressions and legend descriptions (S-parameters or impedances).

parameters.name: Reference impedance / Reference admittance
parameters.description: Normalization for Impedance and Admittance Graphs.

parameters.name: Coloring and Style, Legends
parameters.description: Line markers, color expressions (e.g. emw.freq).

tools.notes: Smith plots require the RF Module. The Smith Plot Group itself is catalogued with the polar plot group.

tools.name: Radiation Pattern (Export)
tools.description: Export node that samples a far-field expression over elevation and azimuth angles (optionally restricted ranges, on a unit sphere or a sphere of given center and radius) and writes the table to a text file, for use in link-budget tools, antenna pattern comparisons or ray-tracing codes. Only real parts are exported, so complex expressions must be wrapped in abs/real/imag/arg.
tools.usage: Results > Export > Radiation Pattern (or right-click a Radiation Pattern plot > Add Plot Data to Export). API: model.result().export().create("exp1", "pg2", "rp1", "RadiationPattern"); model.result().export("exp1").set("filename", "pattern.txt"); model.result().export("exp1").run()

parameters.name: data / Parameter solution (freq, phi)
parameters.description: Dataset and which frequencies/azimuthal parameters to export.

parameters.name: Number of elevation / azimuth angles
parameters.description: Defaults 10 and 20.

parameters.name: anglerestr
parameters.description: none or manual (theta start/range, phi start/range in degrees).

parameters.name: Sphere (center, radius)
parameters.description: Unit sphere or manual sphere for radius-dependent exterior fields.

parameters.name: Include header / Full precision / separator / If the file exists
parameters.description: Output formatting.

tools.notes: For a 2D-axi model set the Azimuthal angle variable to evaluate once per angle; otherwise an evaluate-once-and-revolve approach is used.

tools.name: Polarization (plot for periodic structures)
tools.description: 1D plot type that draws the polarization ellipses of all diffraction orders of a periodic structure in one diagram, normalized to the current order's efficiency or to the largest efficiency of all orders, with arrow heads showing the sense of rotation. It is created by default for periodic ports when three-component fields are solved and is the fastest way to see polarization conversion by gratings and metasurfaces.
tools.usage: 1D Plot Group > More Plots > Polarization. API: model.result("pg4").create("plz1", "Polarization"); model.result("pg4").feature("plz1").set("normalization", ...); set("showrotdir", true)

parameters.name: planewave (Plane wave)
parameters.description: Predefined order/side expression, Manual (xexpr/yexpr) or None.

parameters.name: normalization
parameters.description: Manual (scale), With respect to current order (default) or With respect to all orders.

parameters.name: centerpos / xcenter / ycenter
parameters.description: Auto or user-defined ellipse center.

parameters.name: showrotdir
parameters.description: Show direction of rotation (on by default).

tools.example:
Default 'Polarization' plots of RF_Module/Tutorials/hexagonal_grating show one ellipse per reflected and transmitted order; change normalization to 'With respect to all orders' to compare efficiencies.
API: model.result("pg4").create("plz1", "Polarization");
tools.notes: Requires the RF or Wave Optics Module. Based on the Jones vector variables.

tools.name: Connecting Lumped Ports to an Electrical Circuit (RF Module)
tools.description: Workflow for field-circuit co-simulation: set a Lumped Port's Terminal type to Circuit and connect it in the Electrical Circuit (cir) interface through an External I vs. U, External U vs. I or External I-Terminal element, which exchanges the port voltage and current with the circuit. This embeds a 3D electromagnetic structure (connector, antenna, cable) as one component of a SPICE-like network with sources, loads and semiconductor devices, in the frequency domain or with Electromagnetic Waves, Transient.
tools.usage: Lumped Port > Terminal type: Circuit; Electrical Circuit > External I vs. U > Electric potential: select the lumped port voltage. API: model.component("comp1").physics("emw").feature("lport1").set("TerminalType", "Circuit"); model.component("comp1").physics("cir").create("IvsU1", "ModelDeviceIV", -1)

parameters.name: TerminalType = Circuit
parameters.description: The port voltage is fed to the circuit and the circuit current is applied as a uniform surface current.

parameters.name: External I vs. U / External U vs. I / External I-Terminal
parameters.description: Circuit elements that accept a voltage or current from the field model.

parameters.name: User-defined couplings
parameters.description: Alternative: pass any voltage/current expression (cir.Xn_v, cir.Xn_i) via coupling operators.

tools.example:
Coaxial cable connected to a resistive source and load:
1. Lumped ports at both ends with Terminal type Circuit.
2. Electrical Circuit: Voltage Source + Resistor + External I vs. U (port 1), Resistor + External I vs. U (port 2).
Application Library: RF_Module/Transmission_Lines_and_Waveguides/coaxial_cable_circuit
tools.notes: 'External' elements act as ideal sources: connecting them in parallel with voltage sources or in series with current sources gives 'The DAE is structurally inconsistent'; add a series or parallel resistor. An unconnected circuit port behaves as a continuity condition.

tools.name: Spot Diagram (Ray Optics plot)
tools.description: 2D plot of where rays traced in a 3D model intersect an image surface, either projected from a Ray dataset or taken from an Intersection Point 3D dataset. It can sort rays into an array of spots by release feature (field angle) or wavelength, filter by wavelength, release index, number of reflections or a logical expression, annotate spots with coordinates, RMS spot size and wavelength, draw an Airy-disk circle and automatically locate the plane of best (RMS) focus.
tools.usage: 2D Plot Group > More Ray Optics Plots > Spot Diagram; or Geometrical Optics > Results = Plot spot diagram. API: model.result("pg3").create("spot1", "SpotDiagram"); feature("spot1").set("data", "ip1"); set("arrangement", "wavelength"); runCommand("createFocalPlaneDataset")

parameters.name: arrangement
parameters.description: release (default), wavelength or single; layout automatic/rectangular, columns, paddinghoriz/paddingvert.

parameters.name: Filters
parameters.description: filterwavelengthactive/filterwavelength (632.8 nm)/filterwavelengthtol, filterreleaseactive/filterrelease, numberofreflectionsactive, additionallogicalexpressionactive.

parameters.name: Focal Plane Orientation
parameters.description: normal: directionbased (default), positionbased or userdefined (normalexpr); Create/Recompute Focal Plane Dataset.

parameters.name: Annotations
parameters.description: spotcoordsactive, spotsizeactive, circleactive with circleradiusexpr (e.g. Airy radius).

tools.notes: Requires the Ray Optics Module and a 3D ray solution. Automatic focal-plane search fails if rays are stopped before the best focus; replace such walls by Pass through.

tools.name: Optical Aberration Plot and Aberration Evaluation (Zernike coefficients)
tools.description: Result features that quantify the monochromatic aberrations of an imaging system: the optical path difference of rays crossing a Gaussian reference hemisphere (an Intersection Point 3D dataset with Surface type Hemisphere centered at the focus) is fitted by least squares with ISO/ANSI-normalized Zernike polynomials up to order 5. The Optical Aberration plot (2D Plot Group) shows the resulting wavefront error on the unit circle - all terms, higher-order terms only, or selected terms such as primary spherical Z(4,0) - and the Aberration Evaluation derived value lists the coefficients in a table.
tools.usage: 2D Plot Group > More Ray Optics Plots > Optical Aberration; Derived Values > More Derived Values > Aberration Evaluation. API: model.result("pg4").create("oab1", "OpticalAberration"); feature("oab1").runCommand("createReferenceHemisphereDataset"); feature("oab1").set("terms", ...)

parameters.name: Dataset
parameters.description: Intersection Point 3D (Hemisphere) pointing to a Ray dataset of a Geometrical Optics solution with Compute optical path length on.

parameters.name: Filters
parameters.description: Wavelength (default 632.8 nm, tolerance 1 nm), release feature index, number of reflections, logical expression.

parameters.name: Focal Plane Orientation / Reference hemisphere radius
parameters.description: Direction based, Position based or User defined normal; radius default 50 mm (larger than the RMS spot, smaller than the back focal length).

parameters.name: Maximum polynomial order / Terms to include / Length unit
parameters.description: 2-5 (default 5); All, All higher-order terms, or individual terms (z00, z11, z20, z40, ...); coefficients in um by default.

tools.notes: Z(0,0) piston and Z(1,+-1) tilts indicate misalignment, Z(2,0) defocus depends on the chosen image plane (RMS focus by default). Requires 3D and the Ray Optics Module.

tools.name: Interference Pattern (Ray Optics plot)
tools.description: 2D plot of the intensity fringes produced where several rays cross a cut plane, reconstructed from each ray's intensity, phase, polarization and wavefront curvature. It turns a ray-tracing model of an interferometer or thin-film setup into a fringe image without solving the wave equation; the Geometrical Optics interface must compute intensity and phase, and the plot needs a Cut Plane dataset pointing to the Ray dataset.
tools.usage: 2D Plot Group > More Ray Optics Plots > Interference Pattern (data: Cut Plane on a Ray dataset). API: model.result("pg5").create("intr1", "InterferencePattern"); feature("intr1").set("originspec", ...)

parameters.name: Origin location specification (originspec)
parameters.description: Manual (x, y, z), By ray index, or At ray of greatest intensity.

parameters.name: Manual x/y range
parameters.description: Size of the rendered region.

parameters.name: Resolution
parameters.description: Grid points per direction (0-1000).

tools.example:
Michelson interferometer: Geometrical Optics with Compute intensity + Compute phase, Ray Tracing study, Cut Plane at the detector, then Interference Pattern to show circular fringes.
Application Library: Ray_Optics_Module/Spectrometers_and_Monochromators/michelson_interferometer
tools.notes: The region plotted must be small compared with the wavefront radii of curvature (each ray represents a small wavefront patch).

tools.name: Ray (1D Plot, Ray Optics)
tools.description: 1D plot type for ray variables: either an expression versus time for every ray (or a data-series operation such as Sum, Average, Maximum, RMS over all rays, Sum by default), or two ray expressions plotted against each other at selected times. Typical uses are reflectance versus wavelength of a coated surface traced with polychromatic rays, power budgets along a light pipe, or statistics of optical path length.
tools.usage: 1D Plot Group > More Plots > Ray (data must be a Ray dataset). API: model.result("pg6").create("rtp1", "Ray1D")

parameters.name: y-Axis Data
parameters.description: Expression, may mix ray and field variables.

parameters.name: x-Axis Data: Parameter
parameters.description: Solution number (time on x, one line per ray) or Expression (e.g. gop.lambda0).

parameters.name: Data Series Operation
parameters.description: Sum (default), None, Average, Maximum, Minimum, RMS, Standard deviation, Variance (x-axis time only).

tools.example:
Distributed Bragg reflector: polychromatic rays through a 21-layer Thin Dielectric Film stack; Ray plot with y = gop.I/gop.I0 and x = gop.lambda0 at the final time gives the reflectance spectrum.
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Prisms_and_Coatings/distributed_bragg_reflector, antireflective_coating_multilayer
tools.notes: Add a Filter subnode to plot only rays from one release feature or with a given status. Requires the Ray Optics or Acoustics Module.

tools.name: Intersection Point 3D and Ray Bin (ray datasets)
tools.description: Two datasets for post-processing ray solutions. Intersection Point 3D evaluates ray variables where trajectories cross a plane (quick or general), sphere, hemisphere or general surface F(r) = 0 - the input to Spot Diagrams, Optical Aberration, Aberration Evaluation, histograms and phase portraits - with linear or cubic interpolation between time steps. Ray Bin groups rays into bins of an expression (limits, number of bins or tolerance) and replaces each bin by one averaged ray, for example to reduce thousands of rays per wavelength to one trace.
tools.usage: Results > Datasets > More 3D Datasets > Intersection Point 3D; More Datasets > Ray Bin. API: model.result().dataset().create("ip1", "IntersectionPoint3D"); model.result().dataset().create("rbin1", "RayBin")

parameters.name: Surface type (Intersection Point 3D)
parameters.description: Plane (Quick xy/yz/zx or General by three points or point and normal, optional parallel planes), Sphere, Hemisphere (center, axis, radius), General F(r).

parameters.name: Interpolation between time steps
parameters.description: Linear (default) or Cubic.

parameters.name: Ray Bin expression and Bins
parameters.description: Entry method Limits, Number of bins (default 10, equal number or equal width) or Tolerance.

tools.notes: Intersection Point datasets require the Particle Tracing or Ray Optics Module; Ray Bin requires Ray Optics or Acoustics. The 2D analog Intersection Point 2D uses lines, circles and semicircles.

tools.name: Geometric MTF from Spot Data (Kernel Density Estimation and Spatial FFT)
tools.description: Post-processing chain that estimates the geometric modulation transfer function of an imaging system from traced rays: intersection points on the focal plane are collected per release feature in an Evaluation Group, a Kernel Density Estimation dataset turns them into a line spread function (LSFx, LSFy), and a Spatial FFT dataset transforms the LSF into the MTF, plotted as Line Graphs. Selecting 'Plot spot diagram and geometric MTF' in the Geometrical Optics Results section builds the whole chain automatically.
tools.usage: Geometrical Optics > Results > Plot spot diagram and geometric MTF (Plot MTF in single plot group on by default); or manually: Datasets > Kernel Density Estimation (source: Evaluation Group) > Spatial FFT. API: physics("gop").prop("Results").setIndex("Results", "PlotSpotDiagramAndGeometricMTF", 0); model.result().dataset().create("kde1", "KernelDensityEstimation"); model.result().dataset().create("sfft1", "SpatialFFT")

parameters.name: KDE kernel and bandwidth
parameters.description: Gaussian (default) or Parabolic (Epanechnikov); bandwidth Auto (Silverman's rule) or Manual.

parameters.name: Spatial FFT resolution / layout / Mask DC
parameters.description: Automatic or manual sampling, Normal/Periodic/zero padding, DC masked by default.

parameters.name: Evaluation groups per release feature
parameters.description: Labeled 'LSF Data (relg1)' etc.; must be re-evaluated when releases change.

tools.example:
Petzval lens MTF: set gop Results = Plot spot diagram and geometric MTF, solve the Ray Tracing study, then inspect the generated LSFx (eg1) KDE and MTFx (eg1) Spatial FFT datasets and the MTF line graph.
Application Libraries: Ray_Optics_Module/Lenses_Cameras_and_Telescopes/petzval_lens_geometric_modulation_transfer_function, planoconvex_lens_orientation
tools.notes: Default plots are set up only once; after adding releases or moving the focal plane, update the evaluation groups (or reset default plots). A geometric MTF ignores diffraction, so it is valid when aberrations dominate over the diffraction limit.
